newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to move sideways, support at $340.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to move sideways, support at $340.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 24--------------
Gold is expected to hold above $340 support on Thursday, underpinned by good buying interest, but is unlikely to make any upside progress, analysts said.
Silver is also set to move sideways, with good support at $4.68, while platinum awaits fresh news on Russian exports
GOLD
Support at $340.00 sharpened on Wednesday and analysts say it should hold at least until Monday's OTC options expiry where interest seems to have accumulated around the $340.00 call strike.
But trading currently remains limited to a tiny $2-$3 range with strong overhead resistance pegged at $342.50.
"People are trying to search for a bottom but we are going to manage to hold above the $340 support," said Magid Khoury, chief precious metals dealer at the Swiss-based Socofinance.
"There will be some protection on the $340 calls. There is good interest at that strike," he added.
But over the medium term, with gold's bearish chart outlook still intact, analysts expect another venture towards the $337.50 low seen last week. If $337.50 breaks, $332 will be on the cards.
For technicals to improve gold needs to overcome resistance at $342.50, then conquer the more solid $345. But this is seen unlikely for now.

Analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff, commenting on Comex futures, expected further weakness in the market, saying increased central bank gold sales and the G7 meeting on the weekend remained the paramount concerns.
At 0745 GMT spot gold was indicated at $340.40/$340.70 an ounce, versus $341.10/$341.60 New York close.
SILVER -
Silver's fortunes are slightly brighter than gold in the near-term, although it too faces a narrow range on Thursday.
"People are still short in silver. That's why we are not going lower than $4.70-$4.68," said Khoury of Socofinance, adding that failure in New York to pierce $4.68 proved strong support there.
Rudolf Wolff's Squires however expected further tests of $4.65.
"Should this level break the next area of support is expected at $4.60," he said.
Silver's gains were likely to be capped at $4.78 in the short term with last week's $4.85 peak being the stronger barrier, analysts said.
By 0745 GMT silver was quoted at $4.72/$4.74 cents an ounce compared with New York's close on Wednesday of $4.74/$4.76.
PLATINUM
Technical points are losing relevance in platinum as the market remains indexed to developments in Russia concerning the platinum group metals (PGM) exports to leading buyer Japan this year.

The market shed more value in late dealings on Wednesday to touch a low of $372.00 in New York, down $3.00 from London's close mainly triggered by long liquidation in anticipation of stops, traders said.
The $372.00 area would now act as nearby support since it also represents a 50 percent retracement.
No fresh news emerged on when Russian officials will resume talks with Japan to start shipments, delayed since December.
By 0745 spot platinum was indicated at $374.00/$375.00 an ounce, 50 cents down on New York's close.
--Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
